advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass the already-parsed snapshot dict (or compiled_state) into the stale-channel predicate instead of re-opening/re-parsing the snapshot file in _is_stale_channel_snapshot.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:264: `with open(os.path.join(ticket_dir, snapshot_filename), encoding="utf-8") as f:` then line 278 calls `_is_stale_channel_snapshot(ticket_dir, snapshot_filename)` which re-opens the same file
src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:180: `json.load(f).get("data", {}).get("source_event_uuids", [])` then line 184 `if _is_stale_channel_snapshot(ticket_dir, snap):` re-parses the same file
Ticket census: store has 550 SNAPSHOT_STALE_CHANNEL findings, so scan cost is amplified by the duplicate parse.
advisory.finding: _is_stale_channel_snapshot re-opens and re-parses the snapshot JSON that its callers have already opened and parsed, doubling per-snapshot file I/O and JSON decoding during scan/plan on the ~550-snapshot remediation target.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the only=='stale-channel' dry-run return the stale-channel selected count (consistent with the live path) rather than the triage-orphan sum.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:375: `triage = sum(len(p["triage_orphans"]) for _, p in flagged)` then line 380 `return lines, triage` — used even when only=='stale-channel'
src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:448-458: live only-mode returns `remaining` = count of stale-channel faults
It is benign today only because mixed faults are refused earlier (line 356-358), so stale-only flagged tickets always have 0 triage_orphans, making the dry-run count coincidentally 0.
advisory.finding: In --only=stale-channel mode the dry-run path returns `triage` as the unresolved count while the live path returns the actual remaining stale-channel count, so the second element of the return tuple means different things for the same mode across dry-run vs live.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a stale (no creation_channel) snapshot has NO retained CREATE and assert it is NOT selected as stale_channel.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:125-128 `return (isinstance(compiled, dict) and "creation_channel" not in compiled and _has_retired_create(ticket_dir))`
tests/interfaces/store/fsck_stale_channel_harness.py:22-24 unconditionally writes `create_name = f"...-CREATE.json.retired"` with no parameter to skip it
ABSENCE: no test constructs a stale compiled_state ticket lacking a retired CREATE and asserts `plan["stale_channel"] == []`; the gate the docstring emphasizes is untested
src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:115-119 `try: ... snapshot = json.load(f) except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError): return False`
ABSENCE: harness only writes well-formed JSON snapshots; no test exercises the malformed/missing-file path
advisory.finding: The `_has_retired_create` gate — the documented false-positive guard that a stale `compiled_state` is only flagged/rebuilt when a folded `*-CREATE.json.retired` remains — has no negative test. The shared harness always writes the retired CREATE and exposes no knob to omit it, so no test verifies that a stale-channel snapshot WITHOUT a retained CREATE is NOT selected by `_repair_plan`/`_is_stale_channel_snapshot` (which would otherwise trigger a no-op or data-losing full-log rebuild).
merged_from: The error branch of `_is_stale_channel_snapshot` (`except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError): return False`) is untested — no test feeds a corrupt or unreadable SNAPSHOT and asserts it is NOT classified as stale-channel.
scenarios: A pre-feature snapshot whose CREATE was deleted rather than folded is scanned by --only=stale-channel
A regression that drops the `_has_retired_create` conjunct would still pass every current test
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a `retired_create: bool = True` parameter to `write_snapshot_ticket` and a test `test_stale_channel_without_retained_create_is_not_selected` asserting `_repair_plan(...)['stale_channel'] == []`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with a clean stale-channel ticket plus a separate mixed-fault ticket asserting the whole run aborts before any mutation of the clean ticket.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:353-358 sets `mixed = True` on any flagged ticket and returns `-1` for the whole run
tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair_heldout.py:18-23 the only mixed test builds ONE ticket `mixed-<fault>` that is stale AND has the fault
ABSENCE: no test seeds e.g. `a-stale` (clean stale) + `b-mixed` and asserts the run aborts (`unresolved == -1`) with `a-stale` bytes unchanged
advisory.finding: The whole-run mixed-fault ABORT is only tested with a single ticket that is itself both stale-channel AND mixed. No test covers a run containing one CLEAN stale-channel ticket plus a separate mixed-fault ticket, so the safety contract that the refusal aborts the ENTIRE run before mutation — leaving the unrelated clean stale ticket untouched — is unverified.
scenarios: Operator runs --only=stale-channel over a store where most tickets are clean stale but one is mixed
advisory.suggested_fix: Seed two tickets (one pure stale, one stale+orphan), run `_repair_run(..., dry_run=True, only='stale-channel')`, assert `unresolved == -1`, `REFUSE` names only the mixed ticket, and the clean ticket's files are byte-identical.
